minutes.headline: Committee says it won't choose between a full-time athletic director and reading interventionists in FY27.
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard a select-board letter on tri-board communication, extensive public comment on reading support and the athletic director's workload, and then held a long FY27 budget workshop covering health insurance, a paraprofessional undercount in FY26, reading interventionists, EL staffing and the bridge program. Members declined to choose between funding a full-time athletic director/trainer and reading interventionists, agreed to make no further staffing cuts, planned to vote their own budget before the town manager's number arrives, and approved (pending edits) an official statement on FY2025 budget variances.

what_happened.line: The committee said it cannot sustain further staffing cuts and would not choose between a full-time athletic director/trainer and reading interventionists in the FY27 budget.
Members plan to vote their own FY27 school budget before the town manager sets her budget number, a change in sequencing from past years.
Any override request would go to the May town meeting rather than a November special town meeting, because November needs a higher approval threshold.
The committee voted to finalize its FY2025 budget variance statement, pending edits sent to the superintendent that do not change its message.
Officials disclosed a paraprofessional staffing gap in the current FY26 budget that had gone unaccounted for, but said the year should still close out okay.

why_it_matters: The choice between a full-time athletic director and reading interventionists is left open, so families may not know until later in the FY27 process which program gets funded.

An override, if requested, would appear on the May town meeting warrant rather than a November special vote, and this cycle's cuts would be discussed in broad categories rather than naming specific positions.
A paraprofessional undercount already found in the FY26 budget is a data gap worth watching for whether it recurs or grows in the FY27 numbers that underlie any override ask.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the items the official minutes actually record — the FY25 variance-statement vote, the "no line-item transfers" finding, the warrant total, and most attendee identities (once captioning errors on names are resolved) — but the official minutes are far thinner than ours on the FY27 budget workshop, recording only that it happened rather than any of the ~15 figures discussed, and they omit several planning decisions (vote timing, cut-discussion strategy, override timing) and one item ours misses entirely (Mr. Yapp's resignation from the committee). The one thing worth double-checking first: our minutes have Dr. Fortuna "addressed informally as Tony," but the official minutes give her first name as Jodi and the chair's first name is Anthony — likely a caption mix-up of who was called "Tony."
